## How to use the code suggestions

Predict the result before opening each **Code suggestion**. These are short
syntax reminders or partial examples, not complete solutions. Adapt them in
the executable R chunk below, finish the task, and explain your result.
Lines starting with `#` are comments; replace any CAPITALIZED placeholders
before removing the `#` to run a template. The suggestions themselves do not run
when you render. Complete tasks in order because later objects depend on
earlier tasks. Optional exercises are not needed for the core report.

```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)
library(lubridate)

# Synthetic teaching data, not real patients.
patient_lookup <- data.frame(
  id = c("P01", "P02", "P03", "P04"),
  arm = c("control", "treated", "treated", "control")
)
marker_wide <- data.frame(
  id = c("P01", "P02", "P03", "P05"),
  marker_w0 = c(4.1, 5.2, 6.0, 4.8),
  marker_w4 = c(4.4, 4.7, 5.1, 4.9)
)
raw_patients <- data.frame(
  id = c(" p01 ", "p02", " P03", "p04 "),
  arm = c(" Control ", "TREATED", " treated ", "control"),
  enrolled = c("2026-09-01", "2026-09-03", "2026-10-01", "2026-10-02"),
  note = c(" first   visit ", " repeat sample", "repeat  visit ", "first visit")
)
```

The lookup is a clean export of the participant IDs and treatment labels.
The raw export above lets you practice recreating that cleaning and adding
dates. Inspect the IDs in both exports before deciding which rows to retain.

by `id`. Compare row counts before and after. Use `anti_join()` in both
directions. Explain the missing arm value. How many rows would an `inner_join()` keep?
If the report instead needs every enrolled participant, which table belongs
on the left? Run that reversed join as `enrollment_report` and inspect it.

> rows will remain? Who will have a missing treatment label?
